recipes.name: Fish Tacos Ultimo
ingredients_raw: 1.5 teaspoons canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce

steps.text: Rub tilapia fillets with 2 tablespoons lime juice and season with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and paprika. Spray both sides of each fillet with cooking spray.
Preheat grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Combine yogurt, remaining 2 tablespoons lime juice, cilantro, and chipotle pepper in a blender. Pulse until sauce is well blended. Set aside.
Grill tilapia on preheated grill until fish is easily flaked with a fork, about 5 minutes on each side.

Heat each corn tortilla in a skillet over medium-low heat until warm, about 1 minute. Divide grilled fish evenly over corn tortillas and serve with cilantro-lime sauce, cabbage, cheese, tomato, avocado, salsa, and green onions.

raw_recipe.headline: Fish Tacos Ultimo
raw_recipe.description: Stuffed with tilapia flavored with zesty lime and spicy yogurt sauce, these fish tacos are the ultimate. Top with cabbage, cheese, tomato, and avocado.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delicious! I took the advice from another review and used lettuce instead of cabbage, and fruity (mango) salsa instead of regular salsa. The sweet and spicy went so well together. It was very flavorful. I omitted the cheese for a fresher taste. I would highly recommend this to anyone looking for a fiesta in the mouth.

This was really good! Don't have a gas grill, so I went 7 minutes per side on my Traeger at 350. Very moist fish! Put too much chipotle in the sauce, so had to cut it with some extra yogurt and a bit of rice vinegar. Used the cabbage and it was awesome! Will definitely make again!

I've been searching for a fish taco recipe that will satisfy my need for abundant flavor as well as pass the test for the picky eaters in my house (everyone else) - this was the one. I made some minor alterations: roasted red peppers in lieu of chipotle, I also cut the fish into long strips then skewered before grilling (this made handling on the grill easier and they also slid perfectly onto the tortilla during assembly. I would give this recipe an extra star if I could.

I made these twice now and they were wonderful. The first time I used the yogurt as the recipe states and we didn't like it as much as when I used ranch dressing in it's place. I made the dressing from a mix and added quite a few peppers since we like things pretty spicy. I also cooked the fish in a skillet instead of on the grill. With the fresh tomatoes, cabbage, onions and avacado it was really a healthy and great tasting meal!

You are absolutely correct, rev'd up chef! Thank you for taking the time to perfect it so that I didn't have to add, subtract or substitute one thing! My children loved it. I will make one suggestion to make the tortilla heating go quicker, spritz each side of tortilla with cooking spray (I used coconut oil), place all tortillas on cookie sheet and bake for 3-5 minutes at 425 degrees. I make fish tacos often but this was the first time I used tilapia. Don't substitute anything, people!

We really liked this recipe! I used my cast iron grill on the stove vs going outside in the heat. Followed the recipe for the sauce but added way more cilantro because we love it. I used the sauce from the peppers because I know our limits but used the full amount called for, it wasn't too spicy, especially once added to the taco. Great served on butter leaf or corn tortilla! I just put out a bunch of toppings and let everyone do their own thing. Will make this again!

Overall, this was an excellent recipe. There didn't seem to be enough yogurt sauce to my liking and I was out of yogurt so I added 1/4 c. sour cream and I really like the flavor this added. I served some tacos with flour tortillas and some with corn tortillas and both were very good. The cabbage gave a nice crunch. I substituted fresh pico de gallo for the tomatoes and really liked it.
Great recipe! I used 2lbs captain cut cod & low fat Greek yogurt. The dressing needed sweetener, so I added 1.5 tsp honey. This was so simple and delicious, thanks for sharing it!

Ended up pan frying on a cast iron skillet, came out great. Even the kids liked it. We also used Mahi Mahi, almost any firm white fish would work. Did not use that much of the spice mix, fearing it would be a little too spicy, but could have used more. The nice thing about the yogurt sauce is that you can add as much or as little adobo sauce and chili's to suite your taste. Will definitely make again!

We made it twice. 
Fresh-off-the-boat tilefish was out of this world but you have to remove bones has you break it apart.
It was raining the second time so we used cod and baked in the oven for ~18 minutes at 425. Also excellent but nothing like the super fresh fish.

We don't have a grill, but we LOVE fish tacos so I'll admit I fried mine, BUT the real star here is the sauce. This sauce was so light, so fresh, and so out-of-this-world that I want to just eat it straight. We left the peppers out of the sauce so we could add them individually, as my husband's taste for spicy and my taste for spicy vary greatly. So, if you're worried about the smokiness, just let everyone do what they want, pepper-wise. That's what great about this - it's easy to do for a buffet-type dinner and everyone gets what they want! Lovely tacos!

Tilapia is cheap, but not the best fish to use for this recipe. If you can spend a little more on your fish, you'll be glad you did. I first made this dish about six years ago. My family requests it every couple months. It's always fresh tasting, with great flavors.
Not a fan and it was definitely the yogurt.
fish tacos delicious
Tasty. Not great enough to be a regular item but pretty good.
I made this and it was so delicious. Did my own little flair and my Hispanic roommate wants me to make it again tol
I will absolutely make this again. My husband loved and II loved it. I didn't use salsa.

These were delicious! Even my daughter who doesn’t like fish liked them. I didn’t have all the ingredients so I subbed a lot and they were still good. I’m looking forward to making them again with the correct ingredients! If you don’t have everything on hand, I used lemon instead of lime, mayo instead of yogurt and dill relish and red pepper instead of the peppers. I thought the lime dressing (that I made incorrectly) tasted odd but it was deee-licious with salsa on the tacos. If you don’t like fish, you could sub black beans.
Great foundational fish taco recipe!
I was very impressed- I will definitely make again. Also great if watching weight .
